# Send an app verification request for a LinkedIn Page

For certain functionality and products, you’re required to associate your app with a LinkedIn Page. The company you select will function as the publisher of the app. You must send an app verification request to your Page super admin who is responsible for approving or denying the request to associate an app with a LinkedIn Page.

Prerequisite:

- You already have an existing app associated with a LinkedIn Page. If you don’t, create a new app before proceeding with this procedure.

To send an app verification request:

1. Go to developer.linkedin.com. 
2. Click My apps in the upper-right corner of the page.
3. Select the required app from the list of existing apps.
4. Click the Settings tab.
5. Click the Verify button.
6. In the Verify company dialog, click the Generate URL button.
7. Click Copy URL and send it to the Page super admin for verification. You can send the URL using email or LinkedIn Messaging.
8. Click the I’m done button to complete and close the Verify company dialog.

Results

- The Page super admin will approve or deny your request when they click on the unique URL sent to them.
- Your name, profile image, current title, and company is visible to the Page super admin during the approval process. If you’re a 1st-degree connection with the Page super admin, they’ll see a notice indicating your connection.
- Your Page super admin has 30 days to verify the app with the unique URL. Once the Page super admin approves the request, the app is verified in your app settings. The unique URL will only expire earlier than 30 days if a Page super admin denies the request. This will invalidate all generated links by any developer on that app.

# Developer application review status definitions

Requests related to Developer Product management undergo an approval review process.

If your product request is currently under review, you may see one of the following status messages listed below in the API Developer Portal, depending on the product and tier you are requesting. You can access the status of your review by selecting Review in progress in the developer portal.

| Status Message | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Access Form Review | We are reviewing your access request form responses. |
| Identity Vetting | We are verifying whether your organization meets our access requirements. |
| App Review | We are reviewing your developer application and screencast. |

| Rejection Message | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Incomplete Access Request Form | Your access request form provided insufficient details to approve your request. |
| Unapproved Use Case | The use case you specified is not an approved use case for the API. |
| Fail Email Verification | We were unable to verify the email address you provided. |
| Fail Organization Verification | We were unable to verify that your organization is a legally registered, active entity. |
| Invalid Company Website | We were unable to verify your organization’s website. |
| Invalid Company Page | The LinkedIn page you associated with your app belongs to a different organization. |
| Organization doesn’t meet our access requirements. | We were unable to verify that your organization meets our access requirements. |
| Invalid Privacy Policy | We were unable to verify your organization’s privacy policy.

|
| Invalid Screencast | The screen recording/screencast you provided does not meet our requirements. |
| Invalid App Name | Your application name includes portions of the LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos. |
| Not in Compliance with Data Restrictions | Your application is not in compliance with the relevant LinkedIn API terms. |

For any questions about the status of your application, please contact our developer support team.

LinkedIn is a business- and career-oriented social networking site with over 500 million registered users.

Before you begin

To use LinkedIn for social login you must:

1. Obtain a LinkedIn developer account from https://www.developer.linkedin.com.
2. Do one of the following:

- Open a previously-created LinkedIn application, and copy the client ID and client secret.
- Create a new LinkedIn application and copy the client ID and client secret.
3. Use the Social Login Dashboard and the LinkedIn client ID and client secret to configure LinkedIn as a social login provider.

# Sign in with LinkedIn

Add LinkedIn OAuth to your Supabase project

To enable LinkedIn Auth for your project, you need to set up a LinkedIn OAuth application and add the application credentials to your Supabase Dashboard.

## Overview

Setting up LinkedIn sign-in for your application consists of 3 parts:

- Create and configure a LinkedIn Project and App on the LinkedIn Developer Dashboard.
- Add your LinkedIn (OIDC) `client_id` and `client_secret` to your Supabase Project.
- Add the sign-in code to your Supabase JS Client App.

## Access your LinkedIn Developer account

- Go to LinkedIn Developer Dashboard.
- Sign in (if necessary.)

## Find your callback URL

The next step requires a callback URL, which looks like this: `https://.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`

- Go to your Supabase Project Dashboard
- Click on the `Authentication` icon in the left sidebar
- Click on `Sign In / Providers` under the Configuration section
- Click on LinkedIn from the accordion list to expand and you'll find your Callback URL, you can click `Copy` to copy it to the clipboard

### Local development

When testing OAuth locally with the Supabase CLI, ensure your OAuth provider
is configured with the local Supabase Auth callback URL:

http://localhost:54321/auth/v1/callback

If this callback URL is missing or misconfigured, OAuth sign-in may fail or not redirect correctly during local development.

See the local development docs for more details.

For testing OAuth locally with the Supabase CLI see the local development docs.

## Create a LinkedIn OAuth app

- Go to LinkedIn Developer Dashboard.
- Click on `Create App` at the top right
- Enter your `LinkedIn Page` and `App Logo`
- Save your app
- Click `Products` from the top menu
- Look for `Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect` and click on Request Access
- Click `Auth` from the top menu
- Add your `Redirect URL` to the `Authorized Redirect URLs for your app` section
- Copy and save your newly-generated `Client ID`
- Copy and save your newly-generated `Client Secret`

Developers using the Supabase CLI to test their LinkedIn OAuth application should also update their `config.toml` to make use of the new provider:

```
[auth.external.linkedin_oidc]
enabled = true
client_id = ...
secret = ...

```

Do reach out to support if you have any concerns around this change.

## Resources

- Supabase - Get started for free
- Supabase JS Client
- LinkedIn Developer Dashboard
